key_insight: OSCAR uses a certified simulator plus iterative LLM escalation to keep searching for better optimization formulations, not just feasible ones.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, local-or-cloud workflow for reliable optimization modeling with lower cost and better accuracy when translating plain-language rules into executable models.
method: Build a labeled offline Simulator to certify feasible/infeasible decisions and compare candidate formulations.
Use Coder and Reviewer LLM calls in an escalation policy that decides which model to query next and when to stop.
Optimize the search for the next certified improvement under uncertainty, with cost-ordered escalation in the known-prior case and a prior-free guarantee otherwise.
evidence_signal: On five benchmark problems, OSCAR reached 95%–100% accuracy with two small open-weight LLMs, whose single-attempt accuracies averaged 29% and 48%, while Codex and Claude Code used 3.1× and 5.8× more tokens on average over five runs.
watch_item: The approach depends on maintaining labeled feasible and infeasible decision examples, and its benefits hinge on the quality and coverage of the certified simulator.
paper_title: OR for AI That Does OR: Routing LLMs up the Escalator inside the OSCAR Framework
